story.title: Tanker Collides with River Cruise Ship in New Orleans, All Passengers Rescued
story.summary: A tanker collided with a river cruise ship docked in New Orleans, causing the vessel to capsize. Approximately 130 people were on board, and all passengers and crew were accounted for after a large rescue operation. More than 30 individuals were hospitalized due to injuries sustained during the incident.

explore_lenses.label: Why did the evacuation become so urgent?
explore_lenses.title: The vessel listed and overturned within minutes
explore_lenses.summary: The danger escalated rapidly after the tanker struck the docked American Heritage during passenger disembarkation. That timing meant some people were still aboard when the vessel began taking on water and rolled over.

claims.text: The American Heritage began listing within minutes of the impact and flipped while emergency workers were still evacuating people.
Nearby tug operators, port workers, police and other responders joined the rescue, while cruise officials used a roll call after survivors reached shore to verify that no one was missing.

points: The American Heritage began listing within minutes of the impact and flipped while emergency workers were still evacuating people.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The public reporting does not yet establish exactly how many people entered the water or the sequence of every evacuation decision.
explore_lenses.note: Researched context; forecasts and viewpoints are labeled and attributed.

explore_lenses.label: Did the tanker lose steering—and why?
explore_lenses.title: A steering problem is an early lead, not a finding
explore_lenses.summary: Coast Guard officials said the tanker appeared to have suffered some kind of steering loss, but they had not identified the underlying cause as of November 14. The tanker manager says its vessel is being assessed and that it is cooperating with authorities.

claims.text: Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said the tanker appeared to have experienced some type of steering loss, while stressing that the exact cause was unknown.
OSM Thome, the Atlantic Asphalt's manager, said the master immediately reported the incident to the Coast Guard and that the tanker was stable at anchor for damage assessments.

points: Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said the tanker appeared to have experienced some type of steering loss, while stressing that the exact cause was unknown.
OSM Thome, the Atlantic Asphalt's manager, said the master immediately reported the incident to the Coast Guard and that the tanker was stable at anchor for damage assessments.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: It remains unresolved whether the apparent steering problem involved equipment, navigation, human actions, river conditions, or another factor.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after the rescue is over?
explore_lenses.title: Investigation, care for travelers and vessel assessments
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate life-safety operation has shifted toward an NTSB investigation, assistance for displaced passengers and assessment of both vessels. Those tracks may proceed separately, with findings on cause likely to take longer than the emergency response.

claims.text: The National Transportation Safety Board planned to investigate the crash; AP reported that its members were initially unable to reach New Orleans because of a nationwide flight grounding.
Mayor Helena Moreno said survivors needed practical support including communication with families, food, hotel rooms and transportation after many lost phones, identification or car keys.
The tanker manager said its emergency-response team was coordinating with authorities while damage assessments were underway.

story_report.summary: A tanker struck a docked river cruise ship in New Orleans carrying about 130 passengers, triggering a large rescue operation after the vessel capsized. All passengers and crew were rescued and accounted for, but more than 30 people were hospitalized with injuries. The American Heritage began listing within minutes of the impact and flipped as emergency workers were evacuating people.

sections.heading: Rescue Operation Accounts for Everyone
sections.body: Nearby tug operators, port workers, police and other responders joined the rescue. After survivors reached shore, cruise officials used a roll call to confirm that no one was missing. Mayor Helena Moreno said survivors needed help contacting family members and obtaining food, hotel rooms and transportation after many lost phones, identification or car keys.

sections.heading: Steering Loss Under Investigation
sections.body: Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said the tanker appeared to have suffered some form of steering loss, while emphasizing that the precise cause was not known. The tanker’s manager, OSM Thome, said the vessel’s master immediately reported the incident to the Coast Guard and that the tanker was stable at anchor for damage assessments. The National Transportation Safety Board planned to investigate, though its members were initially unable to reach New Orleans because of a nationwide flight grounding.

unresolved.text: Public reporting has not established how many people entered the water or the full sequence of evacuation decisions.
Investigators have not determined whether the apparent steering problem involved equipment, navigation, human actions, river conditions or another factor.
No public timetable was available for the investigation, repairs or the American Heritage’s return to service.

related_stories.title: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins Elected Alaska's First Democratic Governor Since 1998
related_stories.summary: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has won the Alaska governor's race, marking the first time a Democrat has been elected to the position since 1998. His victory flips control of the office from Republicans and makes him the youngest governor in Alaska's history at age 37. Kreiss-Tomkins campaigned on issues such as affordability and public school funding.
